title: Grumpy Dogbert Lists Forbidden Cheer-Ups

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I'm grumpy today, so don't even try to talk to me.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: And don't try to flatter me or give me chocolate cake to make me feel better.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: And I guess I shouldn't scratch you behind the ears until you have little leg spasms.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Right. None of that.

setting: Dilbert's living room, in an armchair
situation: Dilbert sits in an armchair reading a newspaper with his feet up while Dogbert announces he is grumpy and forbids Dilbert from trying to cheer him up. Dogbert lists flattery and chocolate cake as banned, then adds that Dilbert should not scratch him behind the ears. Dilbert agrees to none of that.
punchline: Dogbert claims to forbid every way of cheering him up, but his list of banned items is really a hint of exactly how to win him over, especially the ear scratching that makes his leg twitch.
summary: A moody dog rules out every pleasant gesture while cleverly spelling out precisely what would make him happy.

title: Dogbert's Positive Reinforcement Backfires

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: My boss asked me to supervise the department secretary. I don't really know how to manage people...

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Try positive reinforcement. Praise the things he does right. Trust him to make the right choices.

transcript.speaker: Secretary
transcript.text: I forgot to write down your messages, so I just put a bunch of gibberish on little pieces of paper.

setting: Dilbert's office, with Dilbert in a chair and Dogbert as his therapist-style adviser
situation: Dilbert tells Dogbert he has been told to supervise the department secretary and has no idea how to manage people. Dogbert advises praising what the secretary does right and trusting him to make good choices. In the last panel the secretary hands Dilbert scraps of paper, admitting he forgot to take messages and simply wrote gibberish on them.
punchline: Dogbert's advice to trust the secretary's judgment is immediately undermined when the secretary shows his idea of a good choice is faking phone messages with nonsense.
summary: A new supervisor gets management advice about trust and praise, only to find his subordinate covering up a lapse with meaningless scribbles.

title: Dilbert's Tiny Ego Fights Giant Insecurities

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Dilbert's ego vs. his insecurities

transcript.speaker: Ego
transcript.text: C'mon, you coward!!

transcript.speaker: Ego
transcript.text: You may be big, but I'm going to pound you into pudding!!

transcript.speaker: Insecurities
transcript.text: I'm going to faint.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I don't think this will be a children's fable anytime soon.

setting: Abstract blue backdrop representing Dilbert's mind
situation: A tiny, sunglasses-wearing figure labeled 'Ego' taunts and threatens a huge, nervous figure representing Dilbert's insecurities. The giant panics and faints. Dogbert looks at the collapsed giant and remarks that this outcome isn't the stuff of children's fables.
punchline: In the classic David-and-Goliath story the small underdog wins through courage, but here the giant simply faints from fear, so it's a pathetic non-event that wouldn't make a children's fable.
summary: A pint-sized swaggering ego bullies an enormous, timid bundle of insecurities into collapsing, and Dogbert dryly notes it makes a poor moral tale.

title: Geraldo Interviews Dogbert's Cult

transcript.speaker: Geraldo
transcript.text: Today on "Geraldo" our entire show is about a dog who started his own cult!

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Actually, Geraldo, I don't know what you're talking about.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I love live television.

setting: Television talk show studio
situation: A talk show host announces that his entire episode is about a dog who founded his own cult. He then thrusts the microphone at Dogbert, who sits on a chair and claims ignorance of the topic. In the last panel the host stares into the camera with a strained grin while Dogbert admits he just enjoys being on live TV.
punchline: Dogbert, the cult-founding dog, feigns ignorance on the show but gives himself away by admitting he only came because he loves live television, hinting the cult is a platform for publicity.
summary: A sensationalist talk show host puts a dog on air to expose his cult, but the dog only seems interested in the airtime.

title: Accounting Dungeon Promotes Valid Questioner

transcript.speaker: Accounting Head
transcript.text: So... you've come to the accounting department for an explanation of the budget report, aye?

transcript.speaker: Accounting Head
transcript.text: Unchain him, Bradley.

transcript.speaker: Accounting Head
transcript.text: Normally we would torture and kill you for questioning our report.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: But you realized that my questions are valid?

transcript.speaker: Accounting Head
transcript.text: No. I'm promoting Bradley. You're my new analyst.

setting: Dungeon-like accounting department
situation: Dilbert visits the accounting department to get an explanation of the budget report. The hooded head of accounting, who runs the department like a dungeon, says people who question the report are normally tortured and killed. Dilbert hopes his questions were recognized as valid, but he is instead drafted as the new analyst while the creature Bradley is promoted.
punchline: Questioning the budget report is treated as a capital offense, and the reward for being right is not vindication but being forced to take over the unpleasant job of the person who was just promoted.
summary: A hooded accounting boss threatens to execute a questioner of the budget report, then conscripts him into the department instead.

title: IRS Mop-Up Crew Takes Everything

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I always get a warm, satisfied feeling right after paying my taxes.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Sure, it's a sacrifice...

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: But my money goes to support vital public services.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Knock knock

transcript.speaker: IRS Agent
transcript.text: We're the I R S mop-up crew.

transcript.speaker: IRS Agent
transcript.text: We came to take your socks and shave sixty percent of your dog.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Bzzzz

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Remind me to adjust my withholdings for next year.

setting: Dilbert's home, sitting on the floor in his living room
situation: Dilbert, sitting in his polka-dot boxers, talks about how good it feels to pay his taxes and that they fund vital public services. Then IRS agents arrive at his door as a 'mop-up crew' and announce they will take his socks and shave sixty percent of his dog. They strip Dilbert of his clothes, drag him away by his shirt and shave Dogbert with clippers.
punchline: After smugly praising taxes, Dilbert discovers the IRS will take literally everything he has left, and his deadpan response is merely to plan better tax withholding for next year.
summary: A man gushing about the joys of paying taxes is visited by tax collectors who strip him and his dog of what little remains.

title: Bob Doesn't Know Eggs Hatch

transcript.speaker: Dawn
transcript.text: We should think of a name before the egg arrives.

transcript.speaker: Bob
transcript.text: How about Shelley?

transcript.speaker: Dawn
transcript.text: Bob, are you aware that the egg will become a baby dinosaur?

transcript.speaker: Bob
transcript.text: What?

setting: A plain purple background, apparently in the dinosaurs' home
situation: Dawn, a gray horned dinosaur, suggests she and Bob pick a name before their egg arrives. Bob, a green dinosaur, cheerfully proposes the name Shelley, apparently thinking of the egg's shell. Dawn then asks if he realizes the egg will become a baby dinosaur, and Bob reacts with wide-eyed surprise.
punchline: Bob has named the future child after its eggshell because he has no idea the egg will hatch into a baby dinosaur.
summary: A dinosaur couple discuss naming their egg, but the father has chosen a name based on the shell and is startled to learn a baby is coming.

title: Dogbert Questions the Meditation Guru

transcript.speaker: Guru
transcript.text: The secrets of the universe will be revealed if you meditate.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Can't you just tell me the secrets?

transcript.speaker: Guru
transcript.text: To meditate you must clear your mind of all thoughts.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: If I have no thoughts how will I know if I'm meditating?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: And how do I come out of it? I won't be able to think about stopping.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: And shouldn't stupid people be the best meditators of all?

transcript.speaker: Guru
transcript.text: Perhaps you are not ready.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Perhaps you should spend more time with some thoughts.

setting: A grassy mountaintop ledge with rocks and sky
situation: A robed guru in a striped turban sits on a mountaintop and tells Dogbert that meditation will reveal the secrets of the universe. Dogbert skeptically pokes holes in the practice, asking how he would know he is meditating and how he would ever stop. When the guru says Dogbert is not ready, Dogbert retorts that the guru needs to think more.
punchline: When the guru dismisses Dogbert's logical objections as unreadiness, Dogbert turns it around and suggests the guru is the one who should spend more time actually thinking.
summary: A mountaintop sage's pitch for emptying the mind gets dismantled by a skeptical dog who finds the logic of meditation full of holes.

title: Dilbert Panics Over Eye Contact

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I like a man who makes eye contact.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Oh no... Uncontrollable urge to look away... I've got to blink about twenty times.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Why did she have to bring that up?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Aaeeeii!! Gasp. Blink. Blink. Blink. Blink. Blink. Blink. Blink.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I love doing that.

setting: A restaurant table on a date
situation: Dilbert is on a dinner date when the woman says she likes a man who makes eye contact. Dilbert, who finds sustained eye contact stressful, privately panics about an urge to look away and blink. He then flails and blinks wildly, knocking over his glass, while the woman cheerfully says she loves doing that.
punchline: The woman misreads Dilbert's frantic, awkward blinking meltdown as a charming quirk, showing how socially clueless both people are in the dating scene.
summary: A nervous engineer on a date freezes up when his companion praises eye contact, then spirals into a frenzy of blinking.

title: Doctor Calls Dilbert Back for X-Rays

transcript.speaker: Doctor Fishlips
transcript.text: Hello, Dilbert, this is Doctor Fishlips. I was wondering if you could come back for some X-rays.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: X-rays? Is that standard procedure a week after an appendectomy?

transcript.speaker: Doctor Fishlips
transcript.text: A patient from the prison is missing... I'm told this isn't the first time "Tiny Tom" has tried a bold escape.

setting: A hospital or doctor's office, with Dilbert on the phone elsewhere
situation: Doctor Fishlips phones Dilbert a week after his appendectomy and asks him to come back for X-rays. Dilbert questions whether that is normal procedure. The doctor then stands with a police officer and reveals a prisoner named Tiny Tom has gone missing, implying the escapee is hiding inside Dilbert.
punchline: The doctor's real reason for the X-rays is that a missing prisoner may have been hidden inside Dilbert's body during or after the surgery, a ridiculous medical and security blunder.
summary: A surgeon summons a recovering patient back for scans because an escaped convict may have ended up inside him.

title: Car-Phonebooth for Non-Car Owners

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: It's NOT a stupid idea.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: You see, people who don't own cars are missing out on the prestige of using car phones.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: The car-phonebooth is a natural solution... Granted, it uses a lot of coins.

setting: Outdoors against a plain blue background
situation: Dilbert defends an invention to Dogbert, explaining that people without cars miss the prestige of car phones. He then reveals the device: a wheeled booth with a steering wheel and seat that works as a pay phone, and he admits it eats a lot of coins.
punchline: Dilbert's solution to car-phone envy is a ridiculous hybrid of a pay phone and a toy car, and its only acknowledged flaw is the coin consumption, not its obvious absurdity.
summary: An inventor proudly unveils a pay phone built into a fake car so carless people can enjoy the status of a car phone.

title: Dogbert Betrayed By Ed McMahon

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Oh, carp!

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I've been called for jury duty.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Me, too.

transcript.text: Dogs can't do jury duty. How did they get your name?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I've been betrayed by Ed McMahon.

situation: Dilbert pulls a letter from his mailbox and groans, then explains he has been summoned for jury duty. Dogbert, holding his own notice, says he got one too. When Dilbert points out that dogs can't serve, Dogbert explains how his name got on the list.
punchline: Dogbert blames Ed McMahon, famous for Publishers Clearing House sweepstakes mailings, implying his name was sold to mailing lists after he entered a sweepstakes.
summary: A summons arrives for both Dilbert and his dog, and the dog knows exactly which celebrity sweepstakes pitchman sold him out.

title: Cult Security Questions Dogbert's Motives

transcript.text: Bob and Dawn join Dogbert's cult.

transcript.text: Your job is to neutralize anybody who questions my motives.

transcript.text: Actually, we have some questions of our own...

transcript.speaker: Dawn
transcript.text: Or should we just neutralize ourselves?

situation: Bob and Dawn, two dinosaur-like creatures, have joined Dogbert's cult and are put in charge of security. Dogbert tells them to neutralize anyone who questions his motives, and they respond that they have questions of their own. They then offer to neutralize themselves, and Dogbert agrees.
punchline: Dogbert's cult leader paranoia means anyone who questions him must be eliminated, so his own security staff are instantly forced to choose between silence and death, and he calmly asks that their deaths look accidental.
summary: A cult leader hires two security guards to silence all doubters, then calmly signs off on their elimination when they voice doubts themselves.

title: Dinosaur Babysitter Fails Asteroid Test

transcript.text: Dial 911

transcript.speaker: Dinosaur
transcript.text: Dial 911

transcript.speaker: Parent

transcript.speaker: Dinosaur

setting: A living room, with a couple on a couch interviewing a dinosaur in an armchair
situation: A couple interviews a dinosaur for a babysitting job by quizzing him on emergency scenarios. The dinosaur confidently answers every ordinary emergency with 'dial 911'. When they pose an asteroid impact causing an ice age, he has no answer.
punchline: The dinosaur handles every routine emergency easily but is stumped by the very catastrophe that famously wiped out his species, a darkly ironic gag about extinction.
summary: A dinosaur applying to babysit breezes through household crises but freezes when asked about the cosmic disaster that doomed his kind.

title: Blind Date With a Mime

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: How was your blind date?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: She wore too much makeup... and I had to do all the talking.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Maybe she's a mime.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: That would explain her invisible dog.

setting: Dilbert's home or a plain room
situation: Dogbert asks Dilbert how his blind date went. Dilbert complains that the woman wore heavy makeup and never spoke, so he had to carry the conversation. Dogbert suggests she might be a mime, and Dilbert realizes this would explain the invisible dog she brought along.
punchline: Dilbert's date's silence, white-face makeup and imaginary dog all fit a mime, a fact he only recognizes after the fact.
summary: A man recounting a one-sided blind date realizes his silent, heavily made-up companion was probably a mime.

title: Tire Ad Threatens Whole Family

transcript.speaker: Television
transcript.text: You've heard the "other" tire company imply that your child's safety depends on its product...

transcript.speaker: Television
transcript.text: That's nothing. If you don't buy OUR tires your whole stinkin' extended family will croak!!!

transcript.speaker: Television
transcript.text: And don't get too attached to the family dog, either. HA HA HA HA HA!!

setting: Living room, in front of a television
situation: Dogbert sits in an armchair watching a television commercial for a tire company. The ad begins by criticizing a competitor for using fear tactics about child safety, then escalates into threatening that the viewer's entire extended family and even the family dog will die if they don't buy its tires. Dogbert watches silently throughout.
punchline: A commercial that mocks a rival for fear-based advertising immediately tops it with far more outlandish and menacing scare tactics, even threatening the family pet in front of a dog.
summary: A tire commercial scolds its competitor for scaring parents, then tries to out-scare it by predicting doom for relatives and pets.

title: Dogbert Stalls Death With Scrabble

transcript.text: Wait!

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I've never been much of an athlete... Let's play "Scrabble" for my life instead.

transcript.speaker: Death
transcript.text: How much time are you allowed for your turn?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I'll see you in August, Bone Boy.

setting: A bare orange void, then a table with a Scrabble board
situation: Death, holding a scythe and a Frisbee, offers Dogbert his life if he can catch the Frisbee. Dogbert, who is no athlete, proposes a game of Scrabble for his life instead. Death sits down to play and asks how long a turn can last, and Dogbert says he'll see him in August.
punchline: Dogbert plans to take months to play a single Scrabble turn, stalling indefinitely so Death can never collect.
summary: A wily dog dodges the Grim Reaper by swapping a Frisbee challenge for a word game he intends to drag out for months.

title: Forced Into Accounting, Goblin Trainer

situation: Dilbert protests being transferred to Accounting while a black-robed, pointy-hooded figure with a staff tells him the change is irreversible and hands him over to a green goblin-like trainer named Bradley. Dilbert complains that he is developing a bad attitude about the job, and Bradley cheerfully says that means he can skip that part of the training.
punchline: Accounting is portrayed as a sinister dark-magic cult that corrupts newcomers, and the trainer is pleased because Dilbert's bad attitude, normally something to be instilled, has already arrived on its own.
summary: A reluctant engineer reassigned to Accounting gets an ominous wizard-style induction, then learns his sour mood has saved his goblin trainer some work.

title: Computer Predicts Obese Selfish Future

setting: Dilbert's office, then a futuristic scene in A.D. 2190
situation: Dilbert tells Dogbert he has programmed a computer to predict what people will be like in 200 years, based on current trends in today's youth. He lists declining science skills, rising childhood obesity and growing selfishness. The final panel shows the extremely obese future people lounging around, casually discussing a person who exploded and not caring.
punchline: Extrapolating today's youth trends yields a future of grotesquely overweight, dim, selfish people who shrug off a neighbour exploding because it means more food for themselves.
summary: A computer model projecting current youth trends forecasts a bloated, uncaring population two centuries from now.

title: Dogbert Mistakes Flashlight for God

situation: Dogbert floats above the ground in a dream, sees what looks like his own body below, and concludes he has died. He is awed by a beautiful glowing light and decides it must be God. The final panel reveals that Dogbert is asleep in an armchair and the light is Dilbert, in a bathrobe, shining a flashlight on him.
punchline: The divine light Dogbert thought was God turns out to be just Dilbert shining a flashlight on him while he sleeps, hence 'a really big let down.'
summary: A dreaming dog believes he has died and encountered the divine, only to be woken by a man with a flashlight.

situation: Two dinosaur parents stand in Dilbert's home discussing what to name their baby, who is off-panel. Dilbert keeps interrupting to report that the baby is wrecking one room after another, while the parents calmly keep brainstorming names.
punchline: The dinosaur parents blithely ignore Dilbert's escalating complaints about the destruction and settle on 'Rex', the stereotypical dinosaur name, with no concern for the damage.
summary: While Dilbert reports his house being demolished room by room, the unbothered dinosaur parents casually pick a cliché name for their rampaging offspring.

A giant dinosaur wearing sneakers explains that dinosaurs deal with things they cannot understand by destroying them. punchline: The dinosaur's cheerful method for dealing with confusion is destructive denial, mocking the idea of ignoring and smashing what you cannot comprehend.
summary: A puzzled Dogbert asks a towering dinosaur about an inherited gadget and learns that smashing the unknown is the reptilian way.

title: Dogbert's Dinosaurs Teach Robber Honesty

situation: A robber with a mohawk, eyepatch and bat recognizes Dogbert as the useless watchdog from the house he burgled. Dogbert calmly introduces two dinosaurs, Dawn and Bob, who then seize the robber and hold him upside down, apparently over a toilet, while lecturing about honesty.
punchline: Dogbert's dinosaurs give the robber a threatening swirly-style lesson, twisting the 'love means never having to say you're sorry' line into a menacing reminder that honesty means never having to beg not to be flushed.
summary: A thief who mocks a harmless-looking dog finds himself in the clutches of the dog's dinosaur associates, who deliver a violent lecture on virtue.

title: Wild Deer Killed Dilbert, Police Report

situation: A police officer arrives at Dogbert's door to deliver bad news. He explains that Dilbert was hunted down and killed by wild deer. He then adds that investigators suspect a professional hit because no fingerprints were left behind.
punchline: The officer treats the deer like cunning professional assassins, applying crime-scene logic to animals that have hooves and could not leave fingerprints anyway.
summary: A deadpan cop informs Dogbert that his friend was the victim of an apparently expert deer assassination.

He then accuses the boy of spending lots of time pondering firecrackers and reporters. In the last panel Dogbert hangs upside down, singed and smoking, having apparently been blown up by a firecracker.
punchline: Dogbert's accusatory interview provokes the boy into proving the point with a firecracker, leaving Dogbert smoldering and boasting that famed interviewer Mike Wallace never got this treatment.
summary: A microphone-wielding Dogbert grills a kid about explosives and ends up charred and dangling after the boy demonstrates.

title: Garbage Man Reviews Dilbert's Cloning Design

transcript.text: Dilbert went to the compost pile in the sky.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I only notice a few linear math errors.

transcript.speaker: Garbage Man
transcript.text: This design would just create a hologram and a bad chile con carne recipe.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Man, you sure know your garbage!

setting: Outdoors on a curb or street, next to a garbage can
situation: A garbage man notices there is little trash to collect and asks if someone died. Dogbert says Dilbert has died, and the garbage man laments that Dilbert had nearly finished a cloning machine design, judging by his earlier trash. After reading a crumpled paper from the trash, he declares the design flawed, and Dogbert compliments his garbage expertise.
punchline: The garbage man, who only knows Dilbert through his trash, can critique a cloning machine design in absurd detail, showing he knows far more than a garbage collector should.
summary: A sanitation worker mourns a dead engineer's unfinished invention by diagnosing its flaws from discarded papers, to Dogbert's amusement.

title: Dating Brainella Ruins Her Outfit

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Gosh, Brainella, I've never dated a woman as smart as you before...

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Let's just start right in talking about all kinds of smart stuff. C'mon, give me your best shot. I'm not intimidated.

transcript.speaker: Brainella
transcript.text: Not here. If your brain explodes, it'll ruin my outfit.

setting: A restaurant table on a date
situation: Dilbert sits at a restaurant table with Brainella, a woman with a huge elongated head, and admits he has never dated someone so smart. He then boldly challenges her to unleash her best intellectual material, insisting he is not intimidated. She calmly declines, saying his brain might explode and spoil her clothes.
punchline: Brainella's dry reply implies Dilbert's brain could not handle her intelligence, putting him in his place while disguising the insult as concern for her outfit.
summary: A date with a super-intelligent woman goes sideways when Dilbert's bravado is answered with a deadpan warning about the mess his overloaded mind might make.

title: Dogbert Tests Women's Intuition

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I'm thinking of a number between one and ten.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: 5.1362894 ... No, I'll say three.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Wrong! The answer is 5.1362894... I'm beginning to wonder if you're really a woman.

setting: A room with a counter, where Dogbert sits facing a woman
situation: Dogbert conducts a so-called scientific experiment on women's intuition, asking a woman to guess a number between one and ten. She first blurts out a long decimal, then changes her mind and says three. Dogbert declares her wrong, since her first answer was the exact number he was thinking of.
punchline: The woman's first guess was exactly right, but Dogbert dismisses it and questions her womanhood because she doubted her own intuition and switched to a different answer.
summary: A dog tests a woman's psychic gift and then scolds her for abandoning the correct hunch she had at first.

title: Naked Engineer Blames The Force

transcript.text: Herman's Hardware

situation: Dilbert feels himself pulled toward a hardware store and claims an irresistible force is tearing off his clothes. The store clerk calmly says he's heard this excuse from other naked engineers, and another naked engineer is seen walking away in the background.
punchline: Engineers are so compulsively drawn to hardware stores that being stripped naked by an unseen force is a well-worn excuse, and the clerk has heard it before.
summary: A lured engineer strips down on the way to a hardware store and offers an excuse that the clerk has clearly heard from many others.

title: Teaching Elbonia Our Management Techniques

Dogbert worries that Elbonia will become an industrial rival. Dilbert reassures him that he also taught them the company's management techniques.
punchline: Dilbert's reassurance implies that the company's management techniques are so ineffective that they will cripple any competitor who adopts them.
summary: After helping a foreign country build a chip industry, Dilbert calms a worried Dogbert by revealing he also passed on the company's own style of management, which is sure to hold them back.

situation: Dilbert buys a pair of huge pants from Bob, a salesman in a green jacket, who promises they will shrink to fit. Dogbert says he was taken, but Dilbert insists they shrink in the wash. After washing them, they have shrunk to the size of a tiny glove with two fingers.
punchline: The salesman's promise was technically true, since the pants shrank, but they shrank far too much to be wearable.
summary: A shopper trusts a salesman's promise that oversized trousers will shrink to fit, only to find the wash leaves him with something absurdly tiny.

title: Uncle Tim's Compass Only Points North

setting: A desk or table where Dilbert and Dogbert talk, with a thought-bubble flashback to a snowy wilderness
situation: Dilbert shows Dogbert a photo of his Uncle Tim, who got lost and froze to death while camping. Dogbert asks whether he had a compass, and Dilbert says the diary reported it jammed. A thought bubble shows Uncle Tim in the snow, bundled up, complaining that his compass only ever points north.
punchline: The joke is the absurd misunderstanding of how a compass works: Uncle Tim complains that he needs south but the compass only gives north, which is exactly what a compass always does, so his 'jammed' compass was working fine.
summary: A man's frozen relative is revealed to have died because he misunderstood that a compass naturally points north rather than wherever he needed to go.

situation: Dilbert wakes from a nightmare and tells Bob he dreamed that Dilbert was killed by deer and left behind only a chile con carne recipe. Bob replies that it is bad news, and Dilbert realizes the dream was real. Bob, eating from a bowl, adds that the chile con carne is bad too.
punchline: Dilbert's nightmare turns out to be true, and Bob callously piles on by insulting the dead man's chile recipe.
summary: A man wakes from a dream about his own death by deer, only to learn it really happened and his cooking was lousy too.

setting: A dark, dungeon-like accounting department throne room
situation: Dilbert, bound in heavy chains and guarded by a green goblin with a spear, is brought before the black-robed, pointy-hatted head of accounting who sits on a throne decorated with a skull. Unable to tell the figure's gender, Dilbert stumbles over how to address them and finally asks outright. The figure replies that in accounting it doesn't matter.
punchline: The accounting department is so dehumanizing and bureaucratic that individual identity, including gender, is irrelevant there.
summary: A chained Dilbert nervously asks a menacing, robed accounting ruler whether they are male or female and learns that such distinctions are meaningless in that department.

situation: The strip is a mock public-service note for new readers who might confuse a potato-like character with an actual potato. punchline: Dilbert's round, featureless head looks so much like a potato that the strip needs a deadpan identification guide, which absurdly explains that potatoes prefer contact lenses out of vanity.
summary: A mock field guide helps readers distinguish the spud-shaped hero from an actual potato by checking for eyewear.

punchline: People are so preoccupied with global crises that a threatening dog barely registers, leaving Dogbert himself frightened of humans.
summary: A prankster dog tries to terrorize passersby, but they are all too consumed by larger worries to notice him.

punchline: Rather than denying the danger of eating the children, the dinosaur plans to spin his predatory nature as a positive trait by calling himself a "strict disciplinarian."
summary: A job-hunting dinosaur gets warned that his meat-eating nature disqualifies him from childcare, so he decides to rebrand it as a résumé strength.

summary: A broadcast executive is told that canine listeners are offended by opera lyrics, only to learn the unintelligible singing is a real language the dogs apparently understand.

summary: A melodramatic dinosaur scales the house to publicly announce a very small, very silly secret.

punchline: Dilbert flatters himself that he was selected as a leader, but he was actually chosen as a nerd to be the subject of an experiment.

themes: being used as a test subject

summary: A policeman questions an unfazed engineer about a colleague's bizarre death during a denture experiment, and the engineer sees nothing odd about it.

summary: A lounging dog mentally prepares for a grueling schedule that consists entirely of sitting around and snacking.

summary: A man's nervous first date with a brilliant librarian goes sour when her kind-sounding reassurance reveals she finds his talk boring.

summary: A defense attorney tries to win over a jury by claiming that fewer people in the world means shorter queues for everyone.

situation: Dilbert sees a coworker, Helena, and worries because he had a bizarre dream about her the night before. When she says he reminds her of something bizarre, he panics and blurts out the details of his dream, including a cheerleading outfit and miniature horses glued to a couch. Helena then reveals she was only wondering why he has never married, and concludes that his confession explains it.
punchline: Dilbert's guilty overreaction exposes his weird dream for nothing, and Helena realizes it explains why he's still single.
summary: A guilt-ridden man spills the details of a strange dream to a woman who was merely musing about his single status, and his confession answers her question.

title: Dogbert's Sonic Obliterator Post Office Shortcut

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Our top story: A dog with glasses was seen blowing up empty mail trucks with some type of "sonic obliterator."

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Much of the city is in ruins, as the dog blasted through buildings to escape police and National Guard pursuit.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: On the plus side, we have a much better shortcut to the post office.

setting: Dilbert's living room, watching a news broadcast on TV
situation: Dilbert sits watching the TV news report about a dog with glasses who destroyed empty mail trucks and flattened parts of the city with a sonic weapon while fleeing police and the National Guard. In the last panel Dilbert stands beside Dogbert, who holds the sonic obliterator gun. Dilbert makes a deadpan remark about the benefits of the destruction.
punchline: Dilbert, rather than condemning the citywide destruction caused by Dogbert, dryly points out that the only upside is a more direct route to the post office.
summary: A news report reveals that a bespectacled dog wrecked a city with a sonic weapon, and the man watching can only note the convenience of the newly cleared path to the mail.

title: Writing Down the Unwritten Rules

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I've decided to write down all of the so-called "unwritten rules."

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: So far I have "Don't phone after ten P.M." and ... uh ...

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: That's it?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: How about "Don't throw porcupines in a balloon store"?

setting: Office desk, early Dilbert-era workplace
situation: Dogbert sits at a desk with pen and paper, announcing that he is compiling all the so-called unwritten rules. His list turns out to contain only one real item, a rule about not phoning after 10 P.M. When Dilbert asks if that's all, Dogbert pads the list with an absurd rule about throwing porcupines in a balloon store.
punchline: Dogbert, short on real rules, fills out his list with a ridiculous and obviously unnecessary rule, mocking the idea that unwritten rules can be exhaustively documented.
summary: A dog author struggles to fill his rulebook of social etiquette and resorts to a bizarre, absurd entry about porcupines and balloons.

title: Therapist Rejects Dilbert's Dating Question

transcript.speaker: Therapist
transcript.text: Frankly, I'm tired of hearing your little problems...

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I hate my job... I haven't had a decent date in a year... My biological clock is ticking away...

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Would it be unethical to date one of your patients?

transcript.speaker: Therapist
transcript.text: Yes, especially an ugly one.

setting: Therapist's office
situation: Dilbert lies on a couch venting to his therapist, who admits she is bored by his little problems. He complains about his job, his lack of dates and his biological clock, then asks whether it would be unethical to date one of her patients. She answers yes, especially an ugly one.
punchline: The therapist's reply insults Dilbert by implying he is an ugly patient, while also being unprofessionally blunt about her tiredness of listening to him.
summary: A bored therapist responds to her complaining patient's romantic hopes with a deadpan insult about his looks.

title: Automatic Dentures Eat Meat Loaf

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: This is the first lab model of automatic dentures.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: You can program them to eat a meat loaf for you while you sleep ... quite a little time saver.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Weren't you working with Johnson?

transcript.speaker: Unseen Voice
transcript.text: Ooh... bad news about Johnson, sir.

setting: Research laboratory
situation: Dilbert shows a bald, white-coated lab colleague a prototype set of automatic dentures, explaining that they can be programmed to eat a meat loaf for you while you sleep. In the final panel, outside the lab door, the Boss asks whether Dilbert was working with Johnson, and a voice replies that there is bad news about Johnson.
punchline: The automatic dentures apparently ate Johnson, implying the invention is dangerous and the lab's earlier collaborator became its meal.
summary: A lab demo of self-chewing false teeth ends with a grim hint that a former coworker met an unfortunate fate.

title: Revenge Through Boring Work Stories

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Dogbert, we must become vigilantes and punish the man who robbed our house!!

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: It's not justice we seek, it's revenge!!!

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: We must make him suffer.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Tell him one of your stories about work.

setting: Dilbert's home
situation: Dilbert, furious that a burglar robbed his house, tells Dogbert they must become vigilantes and take revenge on the thief. He insists they want revenge rather than justice and that the man must suffer. Dogbert calmly suggests the ultimate punishment: making the burglar listen to one of Dilbert's stories about work.
punchline: Dogbert implies that Dilbert's work stories are so tedious and miserable that hearing them is a punishment worse than any vigilante violence.
summary: A vengeful Dilbert wants the burglar to suffer, and Dogbert proposes subjecting the thief to a dull account of Dilbert's job.

title: Garbage Man Defines Life as Garbage

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Mister Garbage Man, what is life?

transcript.speaker: Garbage Man
transcript.text: Well, Dogbert...

transcript.speaker: Garbage Man
transcript.text: Life is like old cantaloupe rinds wrapped in a faded newspaper and sprinkled with wet coffee grounds.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Life is garbage?

transcript.speaker: Garbage Man
transcript.text: Call me a romantic.

setting: Outdoors on a grassy hillside, where the garbage man is collecting trash
situation: Dogbert asks a garbage man to explain the meaning of life. The garbage man answers with a detailed, poetic description of rotting trash. When Dogbert sums it up as life being garbage, the garbage man calls himself a romantic.
punchline: The garbage man's grim description of life as rotting refuse is, to him, a romantic view, because his profession has shaped his worldview entirely around trash.
summary: A philosophical dog seeks life's meaning from a trash collector, who answers in the only terms his job has taught him.

title: Dogbert Becomes God of Mayonnaise

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: (Dogbert hums contentedly in his chair, music notes floating above him.)

transcript.speaker: Thor
transcript.text: Greetings, Dogbert, I am the god of thunder.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Yip!

transcript.speaker: Thor
transcript.text: I am Thor!!

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Take some athpirin.

transcript.speaker: Thor
transcript.text: We're looking for some new Norse gods to update our image. Your name came up.

transcript.speaker: Thor
transcript.text: It's the same way I got started. I worked my way up from god of static cling.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Hmm... "God of Velcro" looks interesting.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Don't laugh. I put your name in for god of mayonnaise.

setting: Dilbert's living room
situation: A horned-helmeted Thor appears and announces himself to Dogbert, who cheerfully mistakes the thunder god for someone with a headache. Thor explains the gods are recruiting new Norse deities and reveals he rose from being god of static cling. Dogbert browses the list, considers becoming god of Velcro, and then reveals to Thor that he has nominated him for god of mayonnaise.
punchline: After Thor brags about his humble start as god of static cling, Dogbert gets revenge by nominating the mighty thunder god for the absurdly trivial title of god of mayonnaise.
summary: A mighty Norse deity recruits Dogbert as a minor god, only to find himself nominated for a ridiculous condiment-based divinity in return.

title: Miracle Water Spa Has No Customers

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Here's a brochure for my new miracle mineral water spa.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: You claim that the water at our house will make people smart, beautiful and healthy.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: If anybody asks, tell them you don't drink water.

setting: Dilbert's home living room
situation: Dogbert hands Dilbert a brochure for his new miracle mineral water spa. Dilbert notes that the brochure claims the water at their own house makes people smart, beautiful and healthy, which clearly isn't true of Dilbert. Dogbert asks him to tell anyone who inquires that he doesn't drink water.
punchline: Dogbert's marketing claims are so obviously contradicted by Dilbert himself that the only fix is to have Dilbert deny drinking the water at all.
summary: Dogbert's spa brochure promises health and brilliance from ordinary house water, so he coaches Dilbert to hide that he's a living counterexample.

title: Prehistoric Wheel Becomes Marshmallow Roaster

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Prehistoric Dilbert . . .

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: What is it?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I call it "the wheel."

setting: Prehistoric cave dwelling, outdoors
situation: A caveman Dilbert has carved a large stone wheel with a hammer and chisel, and a prehistoric Dogbert asks what it is. Dilbert proudly names it 'the wheel.' In the last panel, the two simply sit roasting marshmallows over the wheel as if it were a fire pit.
punchline: Instead of recognizing the world-changing invention of the wheel, the pair use it as a campfire, showing that people fail to grasp or exploit the true value of an innovation.
summary: A caveman unveils his groundbreaking invention only for his companion and him to treat it as a place to toast snacks.

title: Watchdog Lets Burglar Drive Away

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Dogbert, where's all of our furniture?!!

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Your new cleaning person loaded it into his van and drove away... Oh, and he said to tell you he quit.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I think we need to review your job description as watchdog.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I got his address.

setting: Dilbert's empty home (1990-era early strip)
situation: Dilbert comes home with his briefcase to find the room stripped of all furniture. Dogbert, who is supposed to be the watchdog, calmly explains that the new cleaning person loaded everything into a van and drove off. When Dilbert questions his role as watchdog, Dogbert points out he wrote the thief's address on the wall.
punchline: Dogbert watched the burglary happen and did nothing to stop it, but considers himself helpful because he noted the thief's address, and the cleaner's 'quitting' is treated as a formality.
summary: A guard dog stood by while a hired cleaner emptied the house, then proudly offers the culprit's forwarding address as if that settles things.

title: Awkward Elevator Ride Thoughts

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Riding elevators is so awkward.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Stare straight ahead... Don't breathe... Don't fidget... Don't blink... Arms hang like limp weights...

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I think he's dead.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Above all, act naturally.

setting: Waiting at an elevator in an office building
situation: Dilbert stands next to a woman at the elevator and silently thinks about how awkward elevator rides are. He coaches himself to stand rigidly still, not breathe, and not blink. The woman beside him concludes from his stiff behavior that he must be dead.
punchline: Dilbert's effort to act natural by freezing completely makes him look so unnatural that the woman thinks he is a corpse.
summary: A man so anxious about elevator etiquette stiffens into a statue that his fellow rider suspects he has died.

title: Elbonia Switches to Capitalism Overnight

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Did you hear that the tiny East European country of Elbonia has abandoned communism?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Whoa! Big changes ahead.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Elbonia: Monday

transcript.speaker: Sign
transcript.text: Mud Farm

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Elbonia: Tuesday

transcript.speaker: Sign
transcript.text: My tree

transcript.speaker: Sign
transcript.text: My Mud Farm

transcript.speaker: Sign
transcript.text: My pig

transcript.speaker: Sign
transcript.text: My feet

setting: Dilbert's workplace, then the muddy countryside of Elbonia
situation: Dilbert tells Dogbert that Elbonia has abandoned communism, and Dogbert predicts big changes. The Monday panel shows an Elbonian man sunk in mud next to a pig and a mud farm sign. On Tuesday the same scene looks identical except that everything now carries a label claiming private ownership.
punchline: Switching to capitalism changes nothing in Elbonia except that the villagers now label everything they already had as their own property.
summary: A poor mud-bound nation embraces private property by taping ownership labels onto its pig, tree, farm and even its feet.

title: Witchcraft Date Turns Dilbert Into Frog

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: So... uh... why did you decide to take up witchcraft?

transcript.speaker: Date
transcript.text: It comes in handy.

transcript.speaker: Date
transcript.text: For example, suppose I want to get rid of this annoying fly here.

transcript.speaker: Date
transcript.text: Now be a luv...

setting: A restaurant table during a dinner date
situation: Dilbert is on a dinner date and awkwardly asks the woman why she took up witchcraft. She says it comes in handy and uses an annoying fly as her example. In the last panel Dilbert has been turned into a frog sitting on his chair, and she coaxes him to deal with the fly.
punchline: The date's casual 'example' of getting rid of a fly is a threat in disguise: she has turned Dilbert into a frog so he can eat the fly for her.
summary: A man's innocent question about his date's occult hobby ends with him transformed into an amphibian and put to practical use.

title: Dogbert Protests Fur, Gets Threatened

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: How can you live with yourself? Have you no conscience?

transcript.speaker: Woman in Fur Coat
transcript.text: Oh, big deal... a bunch of minks get bad haircuts and I get a warm coat...

transcript.speaker: Woman in Fur Coat
transcript.text: I'll bet you'd make a nice pair of mittens.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I don't think I reached her.

setting: A city sidewalk outdoors
situation: Dogbert stands on the street holding a 'Fur is Murder' protest sign and confronts a well-dressed woman wearing a fur coat, asking if she has a conscience. She shrugs off the complaint, belittling the minks' fate as 'bad haircuts', then says Dogbert would make nice mittens. Dogbert slinks away with his sign dragging, concluding his protest failed.
punchline: The activist's moral appeal is not only ignored but turned against him, as the fur-wearer threatens to make him into mittens, leading to his deadpan understatement that he didn't get through to her.
summary: An animal-rights picket meets a callous fur wearer who answers his guilt trip by sizing him up as accessory material.

title: Dogbert Rejects the Word Cult

transcript.speaker: Dilbert

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: That word has a bad connotation.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I prefer to think of it as a bunch of morons who have nothing better to do with their lives.

setting: Dogbert's armchair, in a plain room
situation: Dilbert tells Dogbert, who sits in an armchair wearing a crown, that his cult idea has gone too far. Dogbert denies calling it a cult, and when Dilbert points out that Dogbert himself used the word, Dogbert objects to its connotation and offers a different description.
punchline: Dogbert objects to the word 'cult' as too negative, then replaces it with a description that is far more insulting to his followers.
summary: A crowned Dogbert quibbles over terminology, swapping a loaded label for an even more unflattering one about his followers.

title: Headache Pills That Cause Headaches

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Do you have something for a headache?

transcript.speaker: Pharmacist
transcript.text: I'm pretty sure this will do the trick.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Pharmacist
transcript.text: I wonder if he meant something to get rid of a headache.

transcript.speaker: Pharmacist
transcript.text: Nah...

setting: A pharmacy counter
situation: Dilbert, who already has a headache (shown by stars around his head), asks a pharmacist for something for a headache. The pharmacist hands over a bottle of pills that seem to be meant to give him a headache, and Dilbert thanks him. The pharmacist then wonders whether Dilbert wanted a cure rather than a cause, but dismisses the thought.
punchline: The pharmacist interpreted 'something for a headache' literally as something to cause one, then shrugs off the possibility that he misunderstood the request.
summary: A customer asks a druggist for a headache remedy and gets handed a product that may do the opposite, with the druggist casually unbothered by the ambiguity.

title: Dogbert's Personality Cult Bathrobe Plan

setting: Dilbert's living room, with Dogbert perched on the arm of an armchair
situation: Dogbert announces he will found a personality cult in his own honor, collecting followers' money and making them wear bathrobes printed with his picture. Dilbert, sitting in the armchair, suggests branding them and letting them run naked would be cheaper. Dogbert dismisses the idea because his followers are not attractive.
punchline: Dogbert implies his cult members are so unattractive that nobody would want to see them naked, which is why the bathrobes are necessary.
summary: A scheming dog plans a vanity cult and shoots down a cost-saving idea by insulting the looks of the people he intends to fleece.

title: Saturday Turns Despair Into Joy

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Wait... today is Saturday...

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I am the happiest man on the planet Earth.

setting: Dilbert's bedroom, early morning
situation: Dilbert wakes in bed at 6 A.M. and gloomily thinks about another day of pointless work. He then realizes it is Saturday, and in the last panel the bed is shown empty and rumpled as he declares himself the happiest man alive.
punchline: The dread of the workweek is instantly replaced by joy when he remembers he has the weekend off, showing how much he hates his job.
summary: A man waking up dreading work suddenly discovers it is the weekend and feels boundless happiness.

title: Naked in a Garbage Can

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Hi...uh, why am I naked and sitting in a garbage can?

transcript.text: I hope I like the second choice.

transcript.text: ...or you saved a lot of money on an above-ground pool.

setting: Outdoors, next to a garbage can
situation: Dilbert wakes up naked and sitting in a garbage can and asks Dogbert why. Dogbert offers two explanations: Dilbert was killed by wild deer and cloned back to life from his old garbage, or he is using the can as a cheap above-ground pool. Dilbert hopes the second one is the answer.
punchline: Dogbert's second explanation is the mundane, cheapskate one, and it sounds almost as absurd as the cloning story, so Dilbert is left hoping for the lesser embarrassment.
summary: A confused, unclothed Dilbert gets two equally ridiculous explanations from his dog for waking up in a trash bin.

title: Dogbert Rescues Dilbert From Bore

transcript.text: There's always the direct method.

setting: Outdoor path in a neighborhood
situation: Dilbert and Dogbert are out walking when a neighbor named Vernon greets them. Dilbert privately dreads Vernon's boring conversation but is too polite to leave, so Vernon starts in on his favorite episode of Kojak. Dogbert bluntly announces they have to go before Vernon's talk turns their brains to tapioca.
punchline: Dogbert has no qualms about the polite fiction Dilbert can't break, and simply tells the boring person to his face that he is mind-numbing.
summary: A trapped, overly courteous man is freed from a tedious neighbor by his dog's refreshingly rude honesty.

title: Escaped Convict Hiding Inside Dilbert

transcript.text: That's stupid. How would he get out?

transcript.speaker: Police Officer
transcript.text: Ever see the movie "Alien"?

setting: Hospital room
situation: Dilbert, recovering in a hospital bed after an appendectomy, is visited by his doctor and a police officer. They explain that an escaped prisoner may have crawled into his torso during surgery. When Dilbert objects that the man couldn't get out, the officer answers by referencing the movie "Alien".
punchline: The officer's casual reference to the film "Alien" implies the escaped convict will burst out of Dilbert's chest, delivered as if it were a perfectly ordinary medical risk.
summary: A doctor and a cop calmly warn a post-surgery patient that a fugitive may be hiding inside him and will emerge in the most horrifying way possible.

situation: Two dinosaurs ask Dogbert if they can join the cult he is reportedly forming. Dogbert cheerfully admits he needs enforcers to hide the hideous and cynical nature of his organization, and accepts them. The dinosaurs celebrate getting in, with only one of them wondering whether they should ask about the hideous part.
punchline: The dinosaurs are so eager to belong that they cheer being recruited to cover up something hideous, and only belatedly think to question what they have signed up for.
summary: Eager dinosaurs volunteer for Dogbert's new cult and celebrate their acceptance even after he admits the group is something sinister to be hidden.

title: Dogbert Wants Opera Banned

setting: Office desk or conference table
situation: Dogbert sits at a desk writing notes while Dilbert listens silently beside him. Dogbert delivers a mock-serious argument for banning opera from television, citing its foreign-language lyrics and its costumed, loud performers.
punchline: Dogbert applies absurd, self-righteous censorship logic to opera, assuming the foreign language hides obscenity and objecting to Viking costumes and hollering as bad role models.
summary: Dogbert pompously builds a case for keeping opera off the airwaves using ridiculous reasoning about foreign lyrics and Viking-dressed shouters.

title: Cloned Back to Life Absence Report

transcript.speaker: Carol
transcript.text: Dilbert, I need to fill out an absence report for the days you missed work.

situation: Carol, an administrative worker holding a notepad, asks Dilbert why he was absent so she can complete an absence report. Dilbert gives an absurd, elaborate story about being killed by wild deer and cloned back to life by his garbage man and dog. Carol calmly writes down a mundane reason.
punchline: Faced with an outlandish excuse, the bureaucrat simply records the most boring standard category, "sick," showing that paperwork only needs a box ticked, not the truth.
summary: An office clerk collecting details for a leave form hears a wildly fantastical explanation and unflappably files it under the most ordinary label.

title: Only Room for One Dilbert

situation: Dilbert complains to the Boss that an impostor is trying to steal his job, and the Boss promises to get rid of him. Dilbert then points out a punk-looking man with a mohawk and eyepatch who announces he finished the report. The Boss hesitates to fire him because the impostor actually produced work.
punchline: The Boss values someone who actually delivers a finished report over the real Dilbert, implying Dilbert is unproductive and easily replaceable.
summary: A lookalike-in-name-only rival delivers a completed report, making the Boss reluctant to dismiss him in favor of the real employee.

title: Dogbert Questions the Fast Food Name

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Doesn't "fast" mean not eating?

transcript.text: So how can you have "fast food"?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: And how much would I have to eat before I starved to death?

He first points out that fasting means not eating, then wonders how much he would need to eat to starve to death. Dilbert just keeps eating silently.
punchline: Dogbert applies deliberately literal, absurd logic to the phrase "fast food," ending with the nonsensical question of how much eating it would take to starve to death.
summary: A dog at a burger joint wrestles with the double meaning of the word "fast" and ends up in a ridiculous hypothetical about starving by overeating.

title: Dogbert's Dog License Written Test

transcript.speaker: Dilbert

transcript.speaker: Dogbert

situation: Dilbert takes Dogbert to renew his dog license at the Department of Dogs. Inside, Dogbert sits on a stool at a counter with a pencil in his mouth, filling out a written test and wondering about the consequences of failing.
punchline: The absurdity of a dog having to pass a written exam to renew his license pokes fun at pointless bureaucratic requirements.
summary: A man drags his pet to a government office where the animal must sit an exam just to stay legally licensed.

title: Convict Clinging To Pancreas, Suspend Disbelief

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Note: Sometimes it is necessary to suspend disbelief for the purpose of creating comic situations. Parents should explain to their children that convicts will rarely, if ever, cling to another person's pancreas.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: Ho ho, it appears we have also located our own Nurse Woodmeyer... the tramp!

setting: X-ray lab in a hospital
situation: Dilbert stands in his polka-dot boxer shorts while a doctor and a police officer examine his X-ray, which shows a tiny convict clinging to his pancreas. A narrator's note then tells parents to explain that this is not realistic. In the last panel the doctor announces they have also found a missing nurse inside Dilbert.
punchline: The strip breaks the fourth wall with a mock parental advisory about suspending disbelief, then piles on more absurdity by revealing a nurse hidden inside Dilbert as well.
summary: An X-ray reveals a fugitive hiding inside a patient's body, followed by a deadpan disclaimer about realism and the discovery of a second person in there too.

title: Dogbert Rubs Lamp, Dilbert Becomes Wiener

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Why are you rubbing that lamp?

transcript.speaker: Sound effect
transcript.text: Rub rub rub

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: It's a routine check for magic genies.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Carry on.

transcript.speaker: Sound effect
transcript.text: Rub rub rub

transcript.speaker: Genie
transcript.text: You have released me.

transcript.speaker: Sound effect
transcript.text: Flash!

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Yes!!! Ha, ha!! Now you must grant me three wishes!

transcript.speaker: Genie
transcript.text: Get real, four-eyes. We don't have a binding contract here.

transcript.speaker: Genie
transcript.text: I like living in a lamp. You disturbed me. I'm going to turn you into a wiener and go home.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: At least it's an experience I can relish.

setting: Dilbert's home living room, next to a table with a lamp
situation: Dogbert rubs a lamp and claims it is a routine check for magic genies while Dilbert idly lets him carry on. A genie emerges, and Dogbert demands three wishes, but the genie refuses because there is no binding contract and says he liked living in the lamp. As punishment for being disturbed, the genie turns Dilbert into a wiener.
punchline: Dilbert, now a hot dog, wryly notes that being a wiener is at least an experience he can 'relish,' a condiment pun, while the genie's 'no binding contract' excuse mocks contract loopholes.
summary: A pet's wish-hunting scheme backfires when the grumpy genie declines to grant anything and instead transforms the bystander into a frankfurter.

title: Dogbert the Substitute Teacher

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Can't I talk you out of becoming a substitute teacher?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Don't worry.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I won't damage the little tykes.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Day one

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Good morning, children. I'm Mr. Dogbert.

transcript.speaker: Student
transcript.text: Are you flammable?

setting: Dilbert's living room, then a school classroom
situation: Dilbert asks Dogbert to reconsider becoming a substitute teacher, and Dogbert reassures him that he won't harm the children. On his first day in the classroom, a student's question reveals that the children are the ones planning to harm him.
punchline: Dogbert promises not to damage the kids, but the kids immediately ask if he is flammable, implying they intend to set the substitute on fire.
summary: A reassuring promise from a would-be substitute teacher is undercut when his first pupil asks a worryingly pyromaniac question.

title: Nordstrom Parody: Buying a Pen

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Nerdstrom

transcript.speaker: Larry
transcript.text: Hi, I'm Larry, and I'll be your personal shopping assistant.

transcript.speaker: Larry
transcript.text: I'll start by measuring you, then I'll do your colors, then compile a brief family history for our records.

transcript.speaker: Larry
transcript.text: Complimentary food and beverages will be served, and a masseuse is on call.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'm looking for a new pen... maybe something in a Bic.

transcript.speaker: Larry
transcript.text: I recommend the blue. We guarantee it for life.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Yes, this will do nicely.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Was it expensive?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Fortunately, I qualified for their indentured servant plan.

setting: A high-end department store called Nerdstrom, then Dilbert's home
situation: Dilbert goes to an upscale store to buy a simple pen and is smothered with absurdly elaborate personal service: measuring, color analysis, a family history, food and a masseuse. He buys a cheap blue pen, and afterward tells Dogbert how he paid for it.
punchline: The over-the-top luxury service for a trivial purchase is so costly that Dilbert had to sign up for an indentured servant payment plan to afford a single pen.
summary: A man who just wants a cheap pen gets pampered by an overeager store assistant and ends up paying for it with years of servitude.

title: Dilbert Shatters Dogbert's Starry Comfort

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: No matter how bad the day is, the stars are always there.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Actually, many of them burned out years ago, but their light is just now reaching Earth.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Thank you for shattering my comfortable misconception.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: It's the miracle of science.

setting: Outdoors at night, sitting on a stone wall under a starry sky
situation: Dilbert and Dogbert sit on a wall gazing at the stars. Dogbert offers a comforting thought about the stars always being there, and Dilbert corrects him with the fact that many stars have burned out and only their old light is still arriving. Dogbert sarcastically thanks him for ruining the thought.
punchline: Dilbert's pedantic scientific correction destroys Dogbert's consoling idea, and he cheerfully presents this as a benefit of science, while Dogbert's thanks is pure sarcasm.
summary: A quiet moment of stargazing turns sour when a well-meant bit of reassurance gets undone by an astronomy fact.

title: Head Sucked Into Torso

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Dogbert, could you give me a hand?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: "Paw"

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I pulled a loose thread on my shirt and my head got sucked into my torso.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: What should we do?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: This might be a good time for a family portrait.

setting: Dilbert's home
situation: Dilbert walks around headless and asks Dogbert to give him a hand, and Dogbert responds by offering a paw. Dilbert explains that pulling a loose thread on his shirt made his head get sucked into his torso. When he asks what they should do, Dogbert suggests it is a good moment for a family portrait.
punchline: Instead of helping with the absurd bodily mishap, Dogbert sees only an opportunity to take a quirky, deadpan family portrait.
summary: After a dangling shirt thread causes Dilbert's head to vanish into his body, his dog treats the freak accident as a photo opportunity rather than an emergency.

title: Lab Rat CPR on a Budget

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Yes?

transcript.speaker: Scientist
transcript.text: I'm looking for my escaped lab rat. The trail leads to this house.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Can't you just use another rat?

transcript.speaker: Scientist
transcript.text: No. I'm on a very limited budget.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: What will you do if he dies?

transcript.speaker: Scientist
transcript.text: CPR

setting: Dilbert's front doorway at his house
situation: A scientist in a lab coat shows up at Dilbert's door, saying his escaped lab rat's trail led to the house. Dilbert suggests simply using another rat, but the scientist says his budget is too limited. When Dilbert asks what he'll do if the rat dies, the scientist deadpans that he'll perform CPR.
punchline: The scientist's budget is so tight that he would resuscitate a lab rat with CPR rather than replace it, which is an absurd and darkly funny extreme of cost-cutting.
summary: A researcher chasing down a runaway test animal explains that funding shortages mean he would rather give it mouth-to-mouth than buy a replacement.

title: Doctor Jokes About Unnecessary Surgery

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: How's it look, Doc?

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: You came in just in time.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: I'm way behind in my alimony payments. I'll have to do some unnecessary surgery on you.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: You have a fair number of redundant organs.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Two lungs... Two kidneys... Large and small intestines...

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: And I'm sure you aren't taking full advantage of your pancreas.

transcript.speaker: Doctor
transcript.text: I find that humor helps my patients relax.

setting: Doctor's examination room
situation: Dilbert, sitting on an exam table in his polka-dot boxers, asks his doctor about his X-ray. The doctor jokes that he needs money for alimony and will perform unnecessary surgery, then lists organs Dilbert has two of. Dilbert ends up lying rigid on the table with his feet in the air, anxiously scribbling, while the doctor says it was just humor to relax him.
punchline: The doctor's supposedly relaxing humor about money-motivated unnecessary surgery leaves the patient more terrified than before.
summary: A physician's dark quips about padding his income with needless operations send his patient into a stiff panic, which he claims was meant to calm him.

title: Nerd, Monkey, Nintendo In Space

transcript.speaker: Space Official
transcript.text: You will be with one other ...uh... astronaut in a a private room.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: SHUTTLE

transcript.speaker: Space Official
transcript.text: You two will have no specific duties on this mission. I'll be monitoring you on video.

transcript.speaker: Space Official
transcript.text: A nerd, a monkey, and one Nintendo at zero gravity... pretty risky experiment.

transcript.speaker: Space Official
transcript.text: To be honest, we were running low on good ideas.

setting: Space agency briefing room and shuttle viewing window
situation: A space agency official briefs Dilbert and a monkey, who are dressed as astronauts, about their shuttle mission. He tells them they have no duties except to be watched on video. Two officials then observe them floating in zero gravity with a Nintendo and admit the whole mission was a desperate idea.
punchline: The space program, out of good ideas, is sending a nerd, a monkey and a video game into orbit just to see what happens.
summary: A space agency launches an aimless mission with a computer geek and a monkey, and openly admits the plan was born of idea shortage.

title: Annual Review: Automatic Dentures Invention

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: My boss is giving me my annual review today.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Your biggest accomplishment was the invention of automatic dentures?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: They can eat while you're asleep.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: This long pause could mean anything.

setting: Dilbert's bedroom, then the boss's office
situation: Dilbert mentions to Dogbert, who is sitting on his bed, that he has his annual review today while he knots his tie in the mirror. In the boss's office, the boss reads out Dilbert's supposed biggest accomplishment, automatic dentures, and Dilbert explains they can eat while you sleep. The boss then falls silent, and in a thought bubble worries about what the long pause might mean.
punchline: The boss, who is supposed to be conducting the review, is the one left anxious and unsure what to say, as if the silence were a meaningful test, when really he just doesn't know how to react.
summary: A review of an engineer's greatest achievement turns absurd when he proudly claims a self-feeding denim-free gadget that works during sleep, leaving his evaluator quietly flustered.

title: Dogbert Hears Escaped Laboratory Rat

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: What's that noise?

transcript.speaker: Sound effect
transcript.text: Skritch skritch skritch

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: It sounds like a rat, escaped from a nearby laboratory, chewing a hole through our front door to avoid sure death from a hideous macaroni-and-cheese experiment.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: That's amazing.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: These babies aren't just for good looks, you know.

setting: Dilbert's living room at home
situation: Dilbert hears a scratching noise at the door and asks what it is. Dogbert, relaxing in a chair, instantly deduces that it is a lab rat escaping from a nearby laboratory's macaroni-and-cheese experiment. Dilbert is amazed, and Dogbert smugly points to his ears as the source of his keen hearing while a rat scurries away.
punchline: Dogbert credits his big ears for his uncanny hearing, with the absurdly detailed deduction about the rat's backstory played completely straight.
summary: A dog with remarkable hearing diagnoses a mysterious scratching sound down to the rat's origin and motive, then boasts that his ears do more than look good.

title: Bank Teller Demands Hand-to-Hand Combat

transcript.speaker: Bank Teller
transcript.text: I cannot allow this withdrawal...

transcript.speaker: Bank Teller
transcript.text: Unless you defeat me in hand to hand combat.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: They seem pretty serious about encouraging the use of their automated teller machines.

setting: Counter at the Bank of Ethel
situation: Dilbert tries to make a withdrawal at the Bank of Ethel, but the teller refuses unless he beats her in hand-to-hand combat. In the last panel Dilbert stands bruised and bandaged, with a torn shirt and a headband, while Dogbert sits beside him. Dilbert concludes the bank really wants customers to use its ATMs.
punchline: The bank is so determined to push customers toward automated teller machines that serving them in person has become a violent ordeal.
summary: A customer who tries to use a human bank teller ends up battered, realising the bank would rather he used the machine.

title: Dilbert's Ego Meets Insecurities

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Dilbert confronts his own ego

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: You can't leave me now...

transcript.speaker: Ego
transcript.text: Nobody tells me what to do! I am pure ego force! Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!!

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Maybe you'd like to discuss that with my insecurities.

setting: Abstract, empty purple backdrop representing Dilbert's mind
situation: Dilbert confronts his own ego, a blobby sunglasses-wearing figure, and pleads with it not to leave him. The ego booms that nobody tells it what to do and laughs maniacally. Dilbert then points to his towering, hulking insecurities and suggests the ego take it up with them.
punchline: Dilbert's insecurities are far bigger and more powerful than his ego, so the boastful ego is easily put in its place.
summary: A swaggering personification of Dilbert's ego gets cut down to size when a giant embodiment of his insecurities looms into view.

title: Dilbert's Dull Diary Entries

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: You know, many great men kept diaries.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Not to mention the entire Kirk Cameron fan club.

transcript.speaker: Diary entry
transcript.text: Monday: Woke up. Went to work. Came home. Ate. Watched T.V. and went to bed

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Well, this was both therapeutic and satisfying.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Sometimes it's good to bare your soul like that.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Who the heck is Kirk Cameron?

transcript.speaker: Diary entry
transcript.text: Tuesday: See "Monday."

setting: Dilbert's home
situation: Dilbert announces that great men keep diaries, and Dogbert snidely adds that so does the Kirk Cameron fan club. Dilbert writes a diary entry that is just a list of mundane daily activities, then calls it therapeutic. He then wonders who Kirk Cameron is and writes a Tuesday entry that simply refers back to Monday.
punchline: Dilbert's life is so repetitive and uneventful that his diary entry for the next day is just a reference to the previous one, and Dogbert's mocking comparison suggests diary-keeping is for unremarkable people.
summary: A man starts a journal to feel profound, but his life is so monotonous that day two of the diary is just a pointer back to day one.

title: Staring Is Rude Too, Dilbert

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Ugh... Look at that young couple kissing in public.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Ugh.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: They should realize how impolite it is.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Is it impolite for us to stare at them?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: We're just the victims in all this, Dogbert.

setting: A park bench outdoors
situation: Dilbert and Dogbert sit on a park bench, and Dilbert complains about a young couple kissing in public. Dogbert asks whether it is also impolite for the two of them to stare at the couple. In the final panel Dilbert, still watching, insists they are the victims.
punchline: Dilbert condemns the couple's rudeness while openly staring at them himself, then casts himself as the injured party, which shows his hypocrisy.
summary: A man scolds lovebirds for their public display while he keeps gawking at them and claims to be the wronged one.
